notes: Seven articles queued and read. The Haight music-hub debate, the homelessness/Medicaid story, the Standard's acquisition announcement and the Rob Bonta power-play column name no street address.

findings.description: Mentioned as an example in a trend piece about developers favoring office over housing: Amazon's proposed delivery warehouse at 900 7th Street reached environmental review in February. Not the article's subject.

citation.label: The San Francisco Standard, “Why San Francisco developers keep building risky offices instead of stable housing,” 24 September 2026

raw.text: Amazon in February was able to push its proposed delivery warehouse at 900 7th St. into the environmental review stage

resolution.method: EAS exact match on 900 07TH ST → parcel 3807001; sf-parcels has blklot 3807001 active, 900–960 07TH; the 2025 roll records it as commercial office, built 1974. EAS puts 900, 960 07TH ST on that parcel, so per the directory contract the fact belongs on one page at the lowest, 900. The record spells the street out as SEVENTH; EAS holds the numbered streets as zero-padded ordinals, so this is 07TH.

publish.note: The headline is a general trend piece about developer incentives, not about this building — same pattern as the Corgi/600 20th St. precedent (news/items/sf-chronicle/2026-09-23.json). Carrying it onto a page would misdescribe what the story is about.

findings.description: An LLC controlled by Tony Garnicki bought the Fisherman's Wharf building at 2300 Stockton Street in May for $18 million from the Academy of Art University, financed in part by a seller loan; the Academy of Art filed a notice of default this week after Garnicki missed the 90-day payment deadline. Garnicki intends to convert the former Academy of Art building from offices to condos and has applied to the Planning Department to determine the building's historical status.

extra.proposed_conversion: offices to 70 condos (per December application by an architecture firm)
